utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Case number IT-95-9-T, the Prosecutor versus Blagoje Simic, Milan Simic, Miroslav Tadic, and Simo Zaric.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just a second, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Literally we have received a certain correspondence between the deputy Prosecutor, Mr. Blewitt, and relevant authorities of Republika Srpska with regard to this particular document, Variant A and B. But in fact, we don't have any B/S/C version of this correspondence, and I kindly ask in the meantime if the Defence could be provided with relevant copies so that we can proceed with the cross-examination, I mean, in order to be efficient with it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is that a totally new document? Not the one the Prosecution was supposed to give to the Defence? I would like to hear. It seems to be a new document.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's a new document, actually. Five minutes ago we -- ten minutes we found it on our tables. And no problem with that. We can handle it. But still we have to compare this translation and to see what is the original of this correspondence, which is related to this issue this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The document you have is in English?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Only translation of Serbian document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. You -- what you are saying is the document you have is in English. You want to have it translated into Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Madam President, we found a copy of certain very important correspondence between the Office of the Prosecutor and Republika Srpska authorities. All these correspondence was made from 30 of July, 2001, including 19 November 2001. The bottom line is that the -- our learned colleagues from the Prosecutor are in possession of these documents related to Variant A and B, and virtually we were provided with this correspondence five minutes ago. I call it acts by ambush. But we can handle it no problem. But still we need a Serbian version of this correspondence, because it is not fair to have this bundle of documents without these original letters.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Could I help the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Maybe our learned friends from the Prosecutor can clarify this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I can't say exactly what time, but sometime after 1.00 this afternoon it was brought to our attention that we had received a reply from the Ministry of Justice in the Republika Srpska, Banja Luka as to information they had about the distribution list for the Variant A/Variant B document. I got a copy of this, which is -- the request is dated the 30th July 2001, and that request was provided to the liaison officer in Banja Luka in both English and B/C/S. The reply came in and although the reply is dated the 19th of November, 2001, I don't believe it actually got back into the Prosecutor's Office until an amount of weeks, I don't know exactly the day, but certainly not before we rose at the last session. What I was given was the English translation of the reply from the Ministry of Justice in the Republika Srpska, and I'm now asking the case manager if he can e-mail someone else in the Prosecution's office and ask where -- if there was an original in the B/C/S, where it was filed. What I provided to the Defence is just the document which I got into my hands, as I said, sometime after 1.00 this afternoon and -- I wasn't asked for the B/C/S version before. Maybe Mr. Pantelic didn't have time to say he wanted the original, but it's now been requested, I hope, through e-mail from someone who may know where the original version is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What about the statements we were discussing yesterday?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Those were available, well, last night and they were put in the Prosecution -- or the Defence box this morning before 9.00. When about 12.30 I hadn't heard anything from Defence as to whether or not they wanted to pursue any issues on them, I made contact with the Defence counsel and -- well, we discussed whether or not they were sufficient for their purposes. I believe it's more appropriate for Ms. Baen to put her response on the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All I wanted to know is whether they were made available.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: They were made available and -- before 11.00 this morning, they were available to Defence counsel.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Well, my idea was --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Just to accelerate proceedings, I kindly asked our colleagues to provide us with this B/C/S version of correspondence because we have only English version, and since this is a very important document, signed by the SDS Party of Republika Srpska, as I said, last year, it might be of -- this document might have certain weight and certain impact on these proceedings. So therefore, I was of opinion to ask, in the meantime, during the cross-examination of my colleague Ms. Baen to have these documents, and then I can proceed. Because otherwise we have to postpone this session and to proceed with the other witness. That's a problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: But Ms. Reidy has said she is trying to find out where the B/C/S version is right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then we shall be able to call again, Mr. O'Donnell, I suppose, because otherwise we cannot properly cross-examine him without this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, with respect I don't know whether it may assist the Chamber to inspect this document but I really -- well, it's up to Mr. O'Donnell to testify what he can talk about this, but his name doesn't appear on this, he's not involved in the correspondence, it has nothing to do with his testimony today or what he can testify to. If the -- if Mr. Pantelic wants to make further submissions based on this document or call this person who signed the letter back to the Prosecutor, that's for him and his Defence to make, or he can make submissions to again challenge the evidence with respect to whether or not this document should be admitted. It is not relevant, I would submit, for the cross-examination of Mr. O'Donnell since he has nothing to do with this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You see the problem with this case [Microphone not activated] and particularly with the document [Microphone not activated]. It is important for both parties to remember that the Defence counsel cannot take decisions on their own. They have to get instructions from the accused persons on whatever document is to be discussed, and then they can take a decision as to what how to handle those documents. So that it is a problem whenever documents are given to the Defence at very short notice because obviously they have to get instructions on them, and they can only do so if they understand the documents properly. In the meantime, Mr. Pantelic, your problem has been noted. We wait and see whether we can get the other -- the B/C/S version of the correspondence and see how far we shall go. So Ms. Baen, you can continue with your cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If I may add, Your Honour, please, this document is very closely related to the testimony of Mr. O'Donnell because the OTP and Mr. O'Donnell provided Defence with a certain number of documents including the minutes from the 50th Session of Republika Srpska Assembly and this particular document is also closely related to that. So inevitably we have to have these documents to proceed with the cross-examination, in addition to the words of our learned colleagues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Of course, yes you have to take your Defence according to instructions so we wait and see whether we can get the B/C/S version. Ms. Baen, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. For the purposes of the record, all four Defence teams were given the statements that were referred to in court yesterday. We all received them this morning and have all read over those statements. And this was the first time we've seen these four statements, so just for purposes of the record. But with respect to Mr. O'Donnell, I'd like to now go through these four statements with him very briefly. And again, I appreciate OTP giving us these because this is greatly going to shorten what I have to ask. So I thank them for that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. O'Donnell.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: As I said, I want to go through those four documents. Do you have them in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I don't know how it would be best for the Trial Chamber -- how you would like to keep track of these documents. Do you want me to have them marked or how would you -- because yesterday there was confusion on the documents. I myself was confused because I didn't have a full set of what we were talking about. And so I was wondering how the Trial Chamber would like us to mark these. For identification purposes or --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It's up to you. If you think that you need those documents for your case, then they have to be put in.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Since we were doing an evidentiary hearing, I didn't know if you wanted a different numbering.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. We will use the same sequence of numbering, because otherwise there will be confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Before you begin, Ms. Baen, I'm a little confused. You say you didn't have a set, a full set, of the documents in front of you yesterday. Unless I'm wrong, I believe I heard Ms. Reidy say that four sets had gone to the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I checked with my co-counsel yesterday. He had the set in his hands. I wasn't saying they didn't deliver a copy. I just didn't have it in front of me. I had an old set that wasn't tabbed and numbered as the set that we got today. I had no problem -- they disclosed everything to us. We had the documents I just didn't have it in front of me. She is talking about yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: I'm referring to --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: -- this and this. As I recall, we didn't have tabulated either, but we certainly had them in front, and I presume you could share with your co-counsel.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, so the record is clear, our team and all the other Defence teams did receive a set of documents that the Trial Chamber had in front of them yesterday. I had -- we had previously received these documents from the OTP. I had an older set that didn't have -- there were some new documents they gave us that were included in the set that was given to the Trial Chamber yesterday. I didn't -- I had the wrong -- the old set in front of me and so to avoid confusion, I didn't have the sequence or all the documents in front of me as they were in front of you, and I was not aware that co-counsel had them in his hands. I asked him today. He said he had them. So I have no complaint with -- I wasn't pointing fingers at the OTP. They have been very reasonable, and we worked fine together. That wasn't what I was suggesting. I just want to make sure I got the numbering clear because I myself -- I felt guilty of getting things confused yesterday because I didn't have the proper numbering for the Trial Chamber. That's all. But be that as it may, I guess we need to get a number from the Registry for these new statements that we received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So you can start with whichever one you want to start with. Let's have the title of the document, and then we can have a number.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Well, I guess we should go by ERN number because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Those are distinguishable, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: All right. The first document is a witness statement for the OTP with ERN number 00562529.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Could you just wait. The Registry hasn't got copies. Can we have copies?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Certainly. We have copies with -- would you like copies for the Registry and for the Bench?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And the Bench, yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Sorry, is it easier for the Registry assistant if I hand them up as Ms. Baen calls out the ERN number, or if I give you all four statements and you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think it's better to give the Registry and all of us all the four statements, and then as she calls them out, we give them the ID numbers.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: If Ms. Baen is going to be referring, essentially, to these documents, I do also have a few spare sets for the interpreters. Maybe when the usher is finished he can distribute them to the interpreter's booth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I think we can go ahead. So you call the number first, and then we all know which document you are discussing.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. This is ERN number 00562529. It's a witness statement taken by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Can we have an ID number for it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's P47 ID.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, there should be a slash, because 1, 2, 3, 4. It should be "/2."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I don't think I get what you're saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I don't have an objection to the collective number. That's perfectly right. But until now we had all these numbers with the slashes, and that is why --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Okay. For the accused numbering.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And actually, these are for the Defence. So if we can follow the correct numbering for the Defence.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: I apologise, Your Honours. I was under the impression this was a Prosecution document. It is D27/2. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, if you take a look at D27/2. And this appears to be a witness statement taken by the OTP on November 25th of 1997; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And the name of the person whose statement was taken has been redacted for, I guess, security purposes; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: The statement is taken -- the person whose statement was taken was an employee of the AID; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And when you've -- you've read through this entire statement recently?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Is there anywhere in this statement where the witness gives information with respect to the seizure of PID 3?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Let's move on to a new document, which is also a witness statement with ERN number 00562504.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: First of all, Ms. Baen, I know the Registry did say D27/2 is for identification purposes, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Well, yes, right now at this point. But I did discuss with Ms. Reidy that I would like to offer these into evidence for the Trial Chamber to read. We discussed that this afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Is there any objection from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes. Well, Your Honour, I think that the basic general rule that was set out in the beginning was that all these supporting documentation that would be marked in as -- for ID and that if at a later stage it became necessary to have one of these fully entered into evidence, that would be the purpose. Now, I know Ms. Baen correctly did say to me she would like the Trial Chamber to read through them. I have no objection to her asking the witness on cross more questions about the contents of it. But we would prefer they be marked as ID, as indeed our supporting documentation was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, actually I was going to come back to that later on. Do you have any objection to this one? In fact, to any of the four -- these four statements, so that we decide this once and for all. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours, please, I think we should object to the admission of this material --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: -- on the simple ground that it is difficult to see why it should be admitted if the primary document that it supports is not admitted in the first place. Until PID 3 goes in, why should the supporting document be admitted?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: Now, if you decide that yes, PID 3 should go into evidence, then this document -- if this material would assist you for providing evidence of the weight that you attach to the document, the circumstances in which it was found, and so on, in that case, then of course it might -- grounds for its full admission would exist. But until that happens, with respect, it seems to me that it shouldn't go in. How can the document be relevant other -- to anything other than your assessment of how -- what weight to give to PID 3?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: For that reason, we say it should simply be marked at this stage.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: May I respond to the objection, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Baen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: That's exactly the reason it should go into evidence. He's got the order backwards. You three Judges need to see the supporting documents in order to determine the admissibility of PID 3, and until you can read these supporting documents, you can't make that decision.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber has decided that the statement is to be admitted into evidence. So Ms. Baen, you can continue. That is D27/2.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Now I'd like to move on to the next statement. I guess I should repeat the ERN number. It's 00562504. It's a witness statement taken by the OTP on November 26th, 1997.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's D28/2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And I bet the Prosecution would still repeat the same objection or --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. But I assume the ruling is going to be the same. So maybe for the record, we would like then to revisit the issue of all the documents we used yesterday because it was on the basis of the understanding that separate documentation would have given ID status until --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We'll come to that. But for the time being, we are dealing with D28/2.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, if you'll take a look at D28/2. And tell me, have you had a chance to read this document recently?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And you've read the entire document?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And this is a witness statement taken by the OTP on November 26, 1997, is it not?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And the witness who was interviewed is also an employee for the AID; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: In Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: In looking through this entire statement, is there any evidence this witness gave with respect to the seizure of P3 ID?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. We'd like to move on to the next document. And just formally we're offering that into evidence. I understand what the Court's ruling is, but just formally we're offering that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: The next document is ERN number 00570537. It's also a witness statement taken by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have it numbered, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's Exhibit D29/2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, in looking at D29/2, this is also a witness statement taken by the OTP; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And this was another person working for AID in Sarajevo; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And the dates of the interview were the 21st and 22nd of November, and the 18th of December, 1997; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I have a question with respect to this statement. Have you had a chance to read over this whole statement recently?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Is there any information in that statement with respect to the seizure, the circumstances regarding the seizure of PID 3?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: For purposes of the record, we offer D29/2 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: The next document which we request be marked is ERN number 00562521. It's also a witness statement taken by the OTP.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's D30/2.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, if you'll look at D30/2. The same question: Is this a witness statement taken by the OTP of an AID employee?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And these interviews -- or this interview was conducted on November 25th and 26th of 1997; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And this witness who was interviewed apparently was not only an employee of the AID, this person was involved in the leadership of the operational section of the AID; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: In Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And is it correct that this statement, the only mention of the seizure of PID 3 in this witness statement is on page 5, if you would turn to page 5, please; is that correct? It's -- the ERN number of the page is 00562525?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. In fact, there is only one sentence about the document, the history of document PID 3, where he says in the statement, "The document was found in the main office of Sarajevo SDS party in former," and I can't read the name, "street during the spring of 1992." Actually, then the next sentence applies. He remembers the document very well because it contains a strategy of the party which was already in action. Well, does the document say that -- the witness statement say those two sentences?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does and the next sentence also refers to it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I was just about to get to that. Does it in fact the next sentence say, "I cannot state who the document was found by"?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: The next sentence states, "However, I can state that it was found by an operational officer of the service"?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So nowhere in the statement do we have the information as to who seized PID 3?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The name of the person, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And in fact, this leader of operations says he doesn't even remember who it was; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: There is no information in there as to the circumstances under which the document was seized?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from the general circumstances outlined at the beginning of the section in relation to this particular document, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: There is no mention as to whether or not there was a search warrant executed?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: There is no information as to when it was seized other than spring -- sometime in the spring of 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: There is no information as to where in the main office this document was seized, is there?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, there is not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: For the purposes of the record, Your Honour, we offer this document D30/2 into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. And for the record, I'm sure the same objection would be repeated by the Prosecution for D29 as well as D30.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That would be correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, the AID came into existence formally in 1996; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And prior to 1996, the AID was formerly known as the Bosnian secret police; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was known as state security. I can't say whether it was known as secret police.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: State security. It was known as the state security; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Well, Judge Mumba, I think it's perfectly within the witness's competence to answer about the dealings with the AID and dealings with this institution. Specific facts about the history and exact name and exact title and that is not something that he was called here to testify on, about the -- certainly about their dealings with it, and the relationship in terms of documents, but historical accuracy is, I don't believe, within the competence of this witness and it's not appropriate to put that question to him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, I don't think it's not appropriate. It is appropriate, and the witness can only tell the Trial Chamber what he knows. If he doesn't know, he will say so. Let the witness answer according to what he knows. Yes, Ms. Baen.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'm reading the transcript to see where I am. Just let me repeat the last question and we'll move on.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, so the AID, prior to 1996, was known as the state security; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. O'Donnell, I'd like to do sort of the same thing, very quickly going through the different documents contained in P45 ID that you went through with Ms. Reidy yesterday. If you could put that set of documents in front of you, we will try to move through those in a similar fashion. Just let me know when you have them. We'll roll on. Let me know. Do you have them in front of you?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not have the collection of documents. I have, I believe, all the documents in their original tabulation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I think he can be shown the copy with the Registry --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And also a copy of PID 3, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: My apologies, I thought you were referring to the associated documents. I have the copies of the main Variant A/Variant B document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: That's actually what I'm talking about. I'm sorry if I confused you when I said supporting documents or whatever I said. It's P45 ID, that set.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And then also a copy of PID 3. Okay. Mr. O'Donnell, I want to work through this set of documents, and I would like for you to turn to P45 ID/1 and /2, if you could turn to those? I'm going to ask you for each document in this set of documents, not about the content or the writing, but when you look at the document itself, does it look different in any way from PID 3? Okay? In other words, if there are any stray marks, if there is underlining or circles, there is a different number, okay? So my question right now is, if you will turn to P45 ID/1 and /2, which appear to be the same document, and tell me, on page 1, do you see anything different on page 1 when you compare it to PID 3?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apart from the number in the top right-hand corner, no.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Now, what about the number in the very -- the top in the middle of the page?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, those handwritten notations on the top of the page are different.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes. That's different also from PID 3?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they are.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. And would you turn to page -- the fifth page of both of those documents? Look at those two pages and compare it with the fifth page of PID 3 and tell me if there is any difference between those documents.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The difference is the circling around some text in Cyrillic about a third of the way down the page.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So in other words, there is some handwriting on P45 ID/1 and /2 and there is none on PID 3; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct. One thing I'll just point out is PID 3 I have in front of me is a translation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Oh, well, Your Honours, we request, please, if we could have the B/C/S version. PID 3, I'm sorry, Mr. Usher.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So now that you've had a chance to look at the B/C/S version, if you could compare, tell me if your previous answers were all correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they were.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: All right. Let's move on to P45 ID/3 and /4. Have you found that?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Same thing, could you compare those two documents, which look to be the same -- first of all, let me ask you, do /3 and /4 appear to be copies of the same document?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Now compare /3 and /4 with PID 3, the first page on those documents and tell me what differences do you see, if any.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The differences are the number on the top, right-hand corner, another number -- the number 55, and at the bottom of the page, the cross and the circle around the date.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Would you turn to the next page of that document, /3 and /4, and tell me if you see anything different when you compare it to the second page of PID 3?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Ms. Baen, when you say "anything different," are you talking about the type script or are you talking about any notations made by an individual, such as scratching, underlining and pen marks.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: That's what I said at the beginning, Your Honour. I'm not talking about the contents or the wording. I'm talking about stray marks, circling, handwriting, anything that makes this -- these documents appear different visually than PID 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Are we concerned about that or are we concerned about what's in print? I mean, these documents you know the source from where they came. They may have been handled by an individual who may have put his own individual markings there. So how is that terribly relevant?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Because -- well, I'll tell you, the content seems to be very, very relevant, and I understand why for the Prosecutors when they are trying to authenticate it and show, I guess, the original source of this document. They are trying to tie these documents together. Their theory is obviously that there was one original and that there were many copies distributed. It goes directly to the credibility of this evidence, if all the copies that we have appear to be different than the evidence that is sought to be put -- the document sought to be put in evidence right now, PID 3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: But how does it add up to that? Because, you know, the evidence is that these came from different municipalities, so they were handled by different people apparently. So they have the underlinings, just as you would have notes which you underline and the other Defence counsel may not underline, having similar pages, because you seem to be stressing on that a lot, but I don't see where that's leading you to.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: If there's some changes in the text itself, I think perhaps that's what you should draw attention to. Concentrate on that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I think it was established yesterday there's no difference in the context. The analogy is one that you made, Your Honour, about an artist -- say he makes a portrait. He makes -- he decides to take his original and he wants to make 400 lithographs of that and sell them separately. If you go to an art show and you see two different lithographs that look very, very similar but have different marks on them, the only way to determine what the original is is to compare them with the original. Now, if the artist destroyed the original, there's no way to compare it. You have to compare the copies and determine somehow by some objective criteria what is authentic and what is original. So actually, that's the exercise we're going through right now. It goes to the heart of all this evidence of the OTP comparing PID 3 with all these other "versions."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Well, I think in the example I gave, I was referring to the numbers, firstly and, secondly, not what might happen to those lithographs in long possession. I think they could be defaced or anything else could happen to them. But I think the general idea was to show that they came from one source.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Exactly, Your Honour. There's no way -- that's exactly the issue. There's no way to show that all of these documents came from the same source as PID 3. That's exactly my point. And maybe I'm going about it mechanically the wrong way, Your Honour. I mean, maybe we should just offer all these into evidence. I have to talk to my colleagues before I do that, because I haven't consulted with them about that. But if that will speed things up and help the Trial Chamber, then -- I actually believe that you and I, Your Honour, are on the same page about this. Maybe I'm just mechanically going about it in a way which is not as appropriate as far -- to the Chamber. So maybe I should consult with my colleagues and see if they want to go this other way that might save time. I'm all for saving time on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Just one moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Judge Singh and the rest of the members of the Trial Chamber, I've consulted with my colleagues, and they told me to take my own advice that I gave the witness yesterday, that we focus on PID 3 with the "100" on it. So apparently they're all in agreement with the Trial Chamber, and I'm just -- I need to move on with something else.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, you can put those documents aside. And I want to ask you -- yesterday, while we were discussing how these different transcripts and minutes referred to some version of the A/B variant document, we were -- actually, Ms. Reidy was discussing P46 ID/7 with you. And you said -- actually --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour. Just Ms. Baen, I think this is the set of documents that I think Mr. O'Donnell has said that he mightn't have had in front of him, the binder that indexed 1 through 11 that the Bench had. But before we go on any further and confuse ourselves, I think that should be clear he's got it in front of him.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thanks, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe the usher can give him. Are they already with the witness? That is P46 ID?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The collection of documents are not there, sorry, in front of me. I do, I believe, have all the documents separately that you are referring to. So if you give me the ERN number and some details of the document, I can find it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. That will help. It's P46 ID/7. If you can turn to that. Yesterday, Ms. Reidy was discussing this document with you. And she asked you if you could assist the Chamber in the relevance of this document with respect to Variant A and Variant B. And I believe your answer was that -- well, your answer was "This document is dated 27th December 1992. On page 2 of the translation which is L0027212, it states about halfway down the page, last line" --

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. Could I have a minute to find the document. I've just got the index showing which one is number 7. So if you give me a minute, I'll find the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Sure. Thanks. Just whenever you get it, let me know.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have the document now in front of me. My apologies, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Could you just identify so there's no confusion --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That's what I was about to ask.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So there's no confusion on the numbering, Mr. O'Donnell, could you tell us what the title of the document is.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document, "Minutes from the SDS Trnovo Municipal Board," dated 27 December 1991. The first page starts with L0027211.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one second. Our numbers don't match here. I'm going to ask him one question about this. So if you'll just bear with me one second and make sure we have the right number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe the problem is that the translation one shows a different year. Not 1991, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I think we've figured it out. I hope we finish this hearing sometime. I'm sorry there's confusion.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Have you got it, Ms. Baen?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I think we solved it here. It's actually -- it should be 46 ID/2, and the ERN number at the top of the page is 01901474.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's the one you want to discuss with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, when you've found this document, would you please let me know. I have a couple of questions. We'll move on.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: That's the one showing the date in the left -- top right-hand -- left top corner, 27th of December, 1991.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: At 18 hours.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have that document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: You remember discussing this document with Ms. Reidy yesterday?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And this is entitled "An extract from the Minutes of the 3rd Session of the executive committee of the Bosanska Krupa," et cetera, et cetera; correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yesterday Ms. Reidy asked you what relevance this document had to the -- all the Variant A/B documents; correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And you stated to her yesterday that under the agenda of this document at point 3(A), it's mentioned implementing the instruction on establishing a crisis staff. Further down under 3(A), it states: "The chairman briefed those present on the instruction on establishing SDS crisis staffs in BH and in accordance with the set instructions proposed the establishment of a crisis staff." Is that what your answer was?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'd like to show you a document now --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes. We're just asking that that be marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Perhaps we could have a copy of the document so we could see whether we agree to --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: It's a document you gave us.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, it's a document I gave. I would like to know whether the Defence have -- with the exception of Mr. Blagoje Simic, it's the only document under the exhibit which the Defence have indicated they intend to object to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: I don't understand. You are saying this document which the Defence are now about to discuss with the witness was given to them by the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honours. I believe if you see in the corner, there's a "C27" in handwriting. That corresponds to the Prosecution exhibit list. And in correspondence with the Defence counsel afterwards -- after the start of this trial, they indicated that this document they would be objecting to -- to use or to introduction of.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Well, I guess they have changed their mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: We're not offering it into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. So can we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's D31 ID/ter.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And the Serbo-Croat version?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. It's D31 ID/ter -- ter/2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It's going to be D32/2 ter ID.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Just for the record, I'm sorry, Your Honours. It's D31 ID and D31 ter ID/2. Not D32, but D31. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, D31. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, do you have a copy of D31 ID/ter in front of you -- /2?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The English version is the one which doesn't have a ter.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ter is for the Serbo-Croat version.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Could you read the copy, excuse me, the title of this document?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document is titled, "Extract from the instructions for work of Crisis Staffs of the Serbian people in municipalities."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So you mentioned that the document that Ms. Reidy discussed with you yesterday was relevant to support the existence of the Variant A/B, or legitimacy of the A/B document, because it mentioned the instructions on establishing a Crisis Staff and the instruction on establishing SDS Crisis Staffs in BH, and so you're telling us that that mention in that -- that the mention of that document in this transcript is the Variant A/B document and not the one that you have in front of you; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So is it possible that they could have been referring to this document you have in front of you instead of a Variant A/B document?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I think that's unlikely because the document I've been given is sent out five months after the extract from the minutes of the third session of the executive committee of Bosanska Krupa, which was the 27th of December, some eight days after the Variant A and Variant B document was --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Right. My question to you is: Is it possible that there is a document like this?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think the witness has answered the question to the best of his knowledge. "Is it possible?" I think now calls for speculation which he can't possibly answer, and that is a submission that Ms. Baen is free to make in the final submissions as to whether -- in her whole argument about the admissibility of PID 3. I think the witness has given his answer once and now she's asking him to speculate further.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'm not asking him to speculate. He's here for cross-examination and yesterday, in support of this Variant A and B documents --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Baen, the point is he had already answered your question which you're now saying, "Is it possible?" That's all that Ms. Baen is referring to -- I mean Ms. Reidy is referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: That's all I want him to answer.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Is it possible they could have been talking about another document, yes or no. Is it possible?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Actually, Ms. Baen, I just have one question I'd just like to direct to Mr. O'Donnell. The document D31 ID, has a different title to the one in document P46 ID/2. Do you think that makes a difference? 31 ID says "Instructions for work of Crisis Staffs of the Serbian people in municipalities," and the other document, 46 ID/2, uses the words "instruction on establishing." So one says "establishing" and one says "instructions for work." Do you think you could be of some assistance in giving your opinion based on your knowledge on that, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, I would have to look through the document in detail to be able to give a proper answer, but it would appear that the extract from the meetings of the third session from Bosanska Krupa are establishing a Crisis Staff some eight days after the Variant A and Variant B document is calling for the establishment of the Crisis Staff. So it would appear to me to be more connected with that document than this other document. But of course, the other factor is that this document is 26 of April, 1992, whereas the establishment of the Crisis Staff is five months beforehand. So I don't see how it could possibly be connected to this -- I don't know how they could have established the Crisis Staff in line with this document which came out five months later.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, the one you're saying is dated 26th of April, 1992, is D31/2, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, I want to talk to you now about the quote original unquote of PID 3 that we -- or the OTP had brought to court here yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Before you forget about it, D31, you want it admitted into evidence?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I was just using it for cross-examination purposes, Your Honour. I'm not offering it into evidence at this time, thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Moving on to the quote original unquote of PID 3 that was brought to court here yesterday, sometime back in October of last year, I met with you, and there were a couple of other Defence lawyers there, to view this document; is that correct? Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: At that time, you basically went through the same procedure of putting on the gloves, the protective gloves; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And up until that time that you broke the seal on the document, back in October, you had -- you've had this -- you have had this document back since 1997, the seal had never been broken, had it?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. And the reason you had this quote original unquote, which as you testified is a Xeroxed copy with a handwritten "100" on it, the reason why this was under seal is because you and/or the OTP planned on doing additional testing on it, possibly such as fingerprints or DNA, et cetera; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not exactly, Your Honours. It was to have the possibility of doing that, and therefore maintaining the document in good condition should we choose to do that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: You might want to do some tests on this document to determine who has touched it, who has knowledge of it, maybe even who actually received it, from whatever source; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Ms. Baen, do forgive me, but how do you do that?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: You'll have to ask the investigator. I was a Prosecutor for a long time but I'm not an expert --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: But you must have some idea how that is to be done, if it can be done, before you ask this witness that question, because I can't see that would be possible, knowing the circumstances in which the document was taken, knowing the circumstances in which the document was made, and purportedly the circumstances through which it's issued, I think that's an unnecessary question. Would you like to move on to the next question?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I'm just about done, but I'm actually on the same page with you again, Judge Singh. I was a Prosecutor for quite sometime and I was surprised when, in our meeting, I was told that it was under seal. When I asked why this document had been under seal, he said because we might want to do some fingerprint testing or DNA. That was the first time I had heard of it. So I was kind of on the same page with you. I think that's impossible. So that's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Maybe it was just a thought.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For the record, DNA was certainly never mentioned in our discussion. I also did not say that we planned to do tests on the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. My question for you at our meeting, was it not why are you -- why are you keeping this document under seal all these years and handling it with gloves? And what I was told, was I not, it's because you might want to do some testing on it and fingerprints was mentioned; is that not correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was in the past tense that we may have wanted to, and the conversation, although I can't recall the actual words, was about us having the possibility of doing testing.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Let me ask you this: Why has this document remained under seal -- if the fingerprint tests were past tense, why is it still remaining under seal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is that relevant, Ms. Baen? Is that relevant?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, because this goes straight to authentication.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What? Because of?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: The reliability of the document, it goes to possible authentication of the document and relevance in connection to any of these men in this room, if there is any kind of test possible, which in the past apparently the OTP thought there was, then I need to ask the questions about that to see if there is any possible link to my client. Could possibly be exculpatory information, it actually could be inculpatory, if it links this defendant to the document in any way. I would sure like to know why this important document has been under seal and all the other documents haven't. That's -- and I find it's really, really relevant, and I only have about three more questions and I'm done. I'm hopefully going to be able to sit down. And I think this witness can answer it. I think he has the knowledge to answer these questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I suppose he can go ahead and answer them. I just wanted to find out your explanation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honours, at the time that this document was obtained by myself in 1997, the document had obviously been handled by different people. At that stage, we did not know whether it would be possible, firstly, to do any tests on the document, such as fibre comparison, fingerprinting, or other document examination. But so that we would have the opportunity of doing that at a later date, should we choose to, the document was put under seal and it was placed in evidence. Because we wanted to maintain the document in good condition, the document has remained under seal. Through subsequent inquiries, with the corroboration of the document, in the evidence I've outlined, there have been no tests performed on the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. So my last question is: You're saying from this point forward, the OTP has no plans of doing any tests on PID 3; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, again, I'm sorry, Mr. O'Donnell is here to testify as an investigator. I don't think he can testify whether ever in the future the OTP -- someone else on the trial team can do that. Is she asking him what does he personally intend? Again, depending on investigations, it's just speculation and irrelevant, frankly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Baen, the objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any other counsel?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, but I have just a couple of questions. It will not take too long.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If I may, I have a suggestion. I would follow the spirit of this hearing -- well, I have a Variant A suggestion and a Variant B suggestion, which means that I don't have these originals of documents that we were provided only in English version. Therefore I'm not able to have my cross-examination -- my part of cross-examination in total. If my learned friends can help us, I suggest -- I respectfully suggest that we have a break now. If during that break we could possibly obtain the B/S/C version of these documents, then I will shortly consult my client and we will be ready for this part of cross-examination. And Variant B would be, if it's not possible to find these documents, to have another witness here - we have a list of witnesses - to have him examined in-chief and then later on, maybe Mr. O'Donnell, who is practically here within this building, can come and finish this part of examination. That would be my suggestion. So I ask for your instructions, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, is the document available?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, it's not available -- it's not that it's never going to be available. It's not available right at this moment. I just got a message back saying that the person who believe -- that can find it in archives in the original is currently -- has currently received a message and is looking for it. I don't have it here. But may I just suggest -- I take it and it seems to me an implication from what Mr. Pantelic is saying that in the absence of this B/C/S translation, he has no other examinations on the cross-examination -- no examination -- no questions on cross-examination relating to Variant A/Variant B. It may assist the Trial Chamber if Mr. Pantelic simply inquire of the investigator what -- to what extent he can help either the Chamber or Mr. Pantelic about this letter, this correspondence, and if it does appear it would be useful and it's worth cross-examining him on it, we would then suspend it until obviously Mr. Pantelic has time to read the original B/C/S and take appropriate instruction from his client. Failing that, as I said, we can break, and I'll notify the Senior Legal Officer the minute we have an original B/C/S version. But again, I'm not clear it's essential for the conduct of this trial.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, Your Honours, if I may just add, no, I'm afraid, no, I'm afraid, I cannot proceed with cross-examination without this particular document, so that's my point. And I'm also agreed to have another witness in chief and then in the meantime, the Prosecution can collect all these necessary documents, because I don't want to follow the practice of my learned colleague Ms. Baen to have various areas of cross-examination and then waiting for the other documents. Thank you so much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber is of the view that we stand down this witness, Mr. O'Donnell, until such time that the document sought by Mr. Pantelic is found. Then we can go ahead with the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I just ask would the Chamber be assisted in having a copy of this correspondence, the one that Mr. Pantelic is demanding is important to his cross-examination so that you're fully advised of the nature of this document, and given that he said it's very important to him. We will, of course, immediately inform you the minute the B/C/S version is in our hands. But it may be of assistance so you know exactly the nature of this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The Trial Chamber would rather stand down the witness, wait for the document to be found, and then Mr. Pantelic will decide how best to conduct his cross-examination. It may be that if he gets instructions after the Serbo-Croat document have been seen, he may not even cross-examine. So we cannot see the document at this stage. And for what purpose? To be able to say this is not relevant, that's not possible. We'll go ahead with the next witness, please. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours, please, if I may just assist you, I just want to remind you that you have given us permission to interpose that other witness tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. MR. DI FAZIO: So it's now twenty to 4.00. Do you envisage us attending to this task now and then continuing on this afternoon with this particular witness? Because -- perhaps that's what we can do, and we'll do everything we can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Maybe we'll have our break, and then we -- when we come back, we'll start with the new witness, unless in the meantime the document is found. MR. DI FAZIO: Yes. But if Your Honour pleases, naturally we will do that if that's what the Trial Chamber wishes, but that might lead to even more complications, with respect, because the one -- the witness for tomorrow is not yet here. Okay? Now, Mr. Weiner is going to be leading the next witness in the case. If we start at him this afternoon, it would mean we go with him this afternoon, stop him for tomorrow, while the other one comes in and does his cross-examination, and then continue. And it might be disruptive and -- I don't know. If the Chamber wishes to proceed that way, then naturally. But with respect, might I suggest it might be smoother if we try and finish this -- Mr. O'Donnell today, if possible, do the cross-examination of the other chap tomorrow, and then start Mr. Weiner's witness on -- God willing, on the Thursday. It might be smoother and less choppy.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Less cumbersome. All right. Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, if I -- with all due respect, we understood that that was the initial idea of the Prosecutor, to start the witness, then pause the witness for Wednesday when the witness for the cross-examination comes over, and then continue the examination-in-chief. And that is what we have agreed on. I mean, we would like to proceed as agreed. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. That was the original plan and agreement, actually, that the witness for Wednesday -- if another witness is still on the stand, we may have to interpose. I think we agreed on that. So we will take our break and --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm very sorry --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I think you will want to hear this. To explain, since you don't have the document in front of you, there are three pages of English translation which were given to the Defence before this afternoon. The three pages are two documents. The first page is a very short document dated the 15th of November, 2001. The second document is one dated the 5th of November, 2001. And I have just received the B/C/S version of that longer document. I said it's a -- in B/C/S, it's two pages; it's a page and a bit in the English language. Perhaps I could provide this now to Mr. Pantelic. He can have a look over it. We're still trying to locate the first short document in B/C/S. But he may be able to indicate to us after reading the original B/C/S whether or not we can simply proceed with Mr. O'Donnell this afternoon, rather than break his testimony.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. We will -- you'll be able to discuss that, and then you'll indicate to the Chamber whether Mr. O'Donnell will continue or not when we resume at 16.15 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Your Honours. Cross-examined by Mr. Pantelic:

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. O'Donnell.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Could you tell us, Mr. O'Donnell, what is your current position in -- within the OTP?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Currently I am an investigations team leader, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And prior to this post, you were also in OTP -- working as OTP members in the other positions?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Prior to that, I was an investigator with the OTP.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Since?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Since 1996.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And I assume that you travel very often to Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Currently, no, Your Honours. I have in the past travelled frequently to Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: How frequently, Mr. O'Donnell? Speaking about the period of 1996, 1997, 1998.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I couldn't say exactly, because it depends on the work at the time. But during the period 1996 and 1997, I made frequent trips to Bosnia.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: You're a lawyer by education?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I am an investigator.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes. But my question was: What is your education, actually? What is your background, profession background?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: My professional background is as an investigator with the Australian federal police, having joined about 20 years ago. Before coming to the Tribunal, I was with the federal police. Since joining the Tribunal, I've since resigned.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And during your professional life in Australia in federal police, could you very briefly explain us what was the area of your activities, professional activities?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What's the relevance of that? According to the issue, what is the relevance of that?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, simply I want to know whether this witness is professionally educated to give us some other answers with regard to the, I would say, counterparts of OTP in Bosnia, which is agency AID. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You just ask him the questions which are relevant, that's all. I don't think that what he used to do before he joined the OTP, having given us his professional background, is relevant.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Sir, during your frequent trips to Bosnia, we could agree that you have very frequent and often relations, professional relations, with the members of the AID?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: What is exactly means this abbreviation, AID, could you tell the Chamber, please?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I answered that yesterday. I believe the acronym is the Agency for Research and Documentation in Bosnia. And Your Honours, I cannot be completely sure of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Do you know when this agency was established, founded?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe it was around 1996, but again, my knowledge in that area is very limited.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And are you familiar with the organisation which was the basis, prior to establishment of AID in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: When you say "familiar with it," I've been told what the organisation was, as I stated before, state security, but I'm not familiar with the organisation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: But you know that the basis for AID agency was state security of Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my understanding, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the fact that after the collapse of all mutual institutions in Bosnia, the MOS organisation, which means the Muslim Intelligence Service, was formed?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe I've ever heard of the acronym MOS.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And are you familiar with the fact that currently, and also during the war, of course, in Bosnia, at least two state police operated, on the Bosnian Serb side and on the side of Muslim-Croat federation?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I believe so, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And sir, we could agree upon the fact that I would say not all but majority of intelligence agencies are also in the course of their duties and activities sometimes through the agents making forgeries?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is purely now speculation. Again, I think if we look at the transcript closely and see "majority of intelligence agencies in the course of their duties sometimes make forgeries," it's a completely speculative, abstract question, which I don't think is relevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: I withdraw this question, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Sir, are you familiar with the acronym KOS?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard the acronym before. I have no expertise in that area and cannot tell you about the organisation that that refers to.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So you don't know the name of this organisation?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Did you hear about the former JNA -- or could we agree upon the fact that the acronym KOS is actually the former JNA intelligence service, army intelligence service?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is my understanding, but again, I really do not have knowledge in that area.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And again, we could agree upon the fact that the Bosnian state police was actually Muslim secret police; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: As I stated earlier in my testimony, I don't know whether it was also known as the secret police. My understanding was that the predecessor to the AID was the state security.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. But sir, you are a well-experienced police officer. You are the well-trained investigator of the OTP. Could we agree upon the fact that the state police normally not wearing uniforms, they are operating under cover, yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Again, Your Honour, I can't see -- maybe Mr. Pantelic could address the uniform of the -- the relevance of the uniform in general of state security officers to the admissibility of Variant A/Variant B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic? I think sometimes we are beating about the bush.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic, I wonder whether, just on the note of this service for state security, the witness quite clearly got information on AID and its predecessor in two of the witness statements of the witnesses he interviewed. So he might well have knowledge through his conversations and questions with the witnesses rather than a broader general personal knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I follow your instructions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So Mr. O'Donnell, after analysing a statement that we were provided this morning, you could agree with me that the --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm sorry. Before Mr. Pantelic goes any further, could he make clear what the statement that he received this morning is, so that we all -- so that we as well as the witness could understand what he is being asked to agree with. He just says "a statement we received this morning." It could be one statement or indeed the last document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. He should specify.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Absolutely. Yes. My apologies. I'm speaking about the document D27/2 and then D28/2, D29/2, and D30/2. These are the statements of the agents of the current secret police of Bosnia and Herzegovina given to the -- Mr. O'Donnell. And in these statements --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. Mr. -- According to the description, these are the statements made by the employees of AID.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: AID, yes. My mistake. Sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: In fact, Mr. O'Donnell, I'm speaking about the first statement given to you on 25 -- 25th November 1997. The ERN number is 00562530.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down for the translation. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And can you also give us the identification number.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: It's D27/2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And the ERN number, the page of this statement, it's 00562530.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So Mr. O'Donnell, did you find? Sorry.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have that in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: On this page, actually, you were in contact with the agents -- police agents of AID organisation. And you are in fact familiar that they prior to the work in AID were engaged in state security police of Bosnia. You are familiar with that fact?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And then, Mr. O'Donnell, we are speaking about the document D30/2, which is a statement of 25th and 26th November 1997. The page in question is 00 -- ERN number is 00562522. And this is the paragraph -- it's paragraph 7 and 8.
