And it seems to me that the agent in question who gave you this statement was the member of -- of military intelligence service. And he stated in paragraph 7 and 8 that the sources for all documents related to SDS and JNA were also other parties and also the former Territorial Defence which is later B and H army, in your work.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like object to Mr. Pantelic reading into the record inaccurate references from the document. If he'd prefer the witness to address, he can. But as a question, he's putting inaccurate statements on the record, purporting that they are from the document. And I would object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. Exactly which paragraph --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, the documents is into evidence. We have these documents, so I don't see any particular problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. It's your interpretation of the contents of the document which the Prosecution is objecting to as inaccurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. In order to resolve this situation, I think Mr. O'Donnell can read these two short paragraphs, these few sentences.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And then we shall resolve this matter. Because I choose, I would say, one bypass, shortcut to speed up proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Okay. Mr. O'Donnell, would you be so kind as to read us six -- actually seven and eight paragraph, the -- in the statement.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Please.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Paragraph 7 is as follows: "The documents in the possession of the service were mostly seized in the Sarajevo area during 1992 and 1993. The documents held mainly consisted of former JNA documents and SDS documentation located in official buildings, residences of SDS members, and buildings used by the SDS." Paragraph 8 is as follows: "Documentation was also handed into the service by other parties because we had the legal duty to collect such documentation. The Territorial Defence, which later became the BiH army, submitted a large quantity of documentation, and citizens who found important documents also handed them in."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, could you just bear with me for a second. I have to check these documents. Please.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes. Now, Mr. O'Donnell, I'm speaking about the document D29/2, which is also a statement given on 21st and 22nd November and 18th December, 1997. Unfortunately, I don't see the ERN number here but it is page 2 of this statement. And you can confirm that the agent in question actually was a member of the BH army and also agent of the AID agency; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is correct that he speaks about having been those two things but not at the same time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Please. Could you explain, yeah, of course?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: In paragraph 1, he states that he is an operational worker with the department, within the Sarajevo sector of the AID, that he has held that position since starting with the AID, which is from May, 1994, but then it says, "From the start of the war until May, 1994, I was a member of the BiH army."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Yes. Thank you, Mr. O'Donnell. Now, I'm turning to your list of supporting documents for your testimony. It's actually list of -- consisted of 11 documents, speaking about the various minutes and decisions related to Crisis Staff, various Crisis Staffs in Bosnia. My first question is: Have you ever visited Samac, town Samac, during your activities, professional activities?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe that I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: You know that Samac is in -- on the northern part of Bosnia, on the Sava River?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: We could agree roughly that the distance between Samac and Sarajevo is around 250 kilometres, more or less?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I could not say in terms of kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Do you know what is the distance between Banja Luka and Sarajevo, please?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, I'm sure that if Mr. Pantelic wants this evidence on the record, he could provide a map of which you could take judicial notice of the fact that according to a map there is so many kilometres distance between Banja Luka and Sarajevo. It's a waste of time to continue to ask this witness that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic. You have understood what Ms. Reidy is saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. May I have the assistance of the usher? I have one copy of the map. I don't want to tender it into evidence but I just want to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You can state what the kilometres are.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I want to locate all these places where the alleged document in question was mentioned or found, so just to have an impression of the area, of the area where, in relation to Samac, is, for example, the town of Prijedor or Kljuc or Bosanska Krupa because this is the line of questioning which is important for our case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Well, you can simply mention the places and say, you know, and say -- ask the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Not the distances because that is a -- on the map. We can take judicial notice of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, we could agree on the fact that the towns Prijedor, Bosanska Krupa, Bosanski Petrovac and Kljuc are actually on the northwestern side of Bosnia; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And also we could agree that the town Donji Vakuf is actually north-west of -- well, yeah, north-west of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And also, we could agree that a place named Trnovo is south of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And then the town Tuzla is north-east of Sarajevo -- or rather north; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. By the way, Mr. O'Donnell, have you visited all these places during your missions?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I have not. I have visited some of those places.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So basically, your contact is in Sarajevo in this area of Sarajevo with your colleagues from AID agency; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, I've had contact with people from different parts of Bosnia. Some of the contact in relation to this document has been with officials in Sarajevo, some has been with officials in parts of the west of Bosnia and also with officials from the Republika Srpska in Pale.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. O'Donnell.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Now, Your Honours, I would like to tender into evidence - of course with ID numbers if, according to our practice - the correspondence between the Office of the Prosecutor and the relevant authorities of Republika Srpska, because now I have -- and I would like to thank our learned colleagues. I have also B/C/S versions of this correspondence and also English version, and also enough copies for Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What is the correspondence dealing with?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Correspondence is actually related with the document, alleged document, Variant A and B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. You can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, you -- did you made any contact --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you wait so that we can follow with the numbering?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Although they are stapled together, they seem to have been written at different dates.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I can give --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which one can we begin with.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: In fact, if you want, I could make a reference, but now I'm speaking about a document dated 5th of November, 2001. The -- sent by the Serb Democratic Party main office of Pale to Ministry of Justice of Republika Srpska. I believe it is the fourth page in this bundle of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: It has the Serbo-Croat equivalent -- does it have the Serbo-Croat version?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, Your Honour. It is also in this, I would say, bundle of documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Is it the one numbered on the top, right-hand corner 02162024?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: That's correct, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Can we have the number? You did say you wanted to tender into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes. My suggestion would be, Your Honour, because all this correspondence is related to this particular issue, maybe to have one number, and then, if a party would like to make any reference, there is an ERN number and also there are the dates.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. I think it is better because we are going to have a slash for the number of the accused. Any objection from the Prosecution?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I don't think we have any objection to this specific document. But just consistent with our former objection, we thought that everything would be ID until the former resolution. But specifically to this document, anything different from our former objection, we don't have.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Okay. Can we have it numbered as an exhibit.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The B/C/S version of this document is -- will be Exhibit D23/1 ter, and the English version D23/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: All right. So this is the D23/1. This is the letter from the Republika Srpska Serb Democratic Party main office. And then, Your Honours, I would kindly ask a number for the -- another document, which is the letter signed by Deputy Prosecutor Mr. Blewitt, dated 30 of July, 2001, English and as well B/C/S version, sent to a liaison officer of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can we have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The B/C/S version is D24/1 ter, and the English version is D24/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And finally, Your Honours, speaking about the letter dated 15th of November, 2001. It's a letter of SDS presidency, sent to Ministry of Justice of Republika Srpska, English and B/S/C version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can I have the number, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honours. The B/C/S version will be D25/1 ter, and the English version will be Exhibit D25/1.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. O'Donnell, speaking about the document D23/1, did you have any official contact during your missions in Bosnia with Ms. Rajka Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: On which occasion you were in professional conduct was Ms. Rajka Stanisic. Could you tell the Chamber, please.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, at the end of 1997 and the beginning of 1998, I spoke with Ms. Stanisic in Pale.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: What was the reason to speak with Ms. Rajka Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Myself and other members of the Office of the Prosecutor were in Pale on an official mission to the Republika Srpska government and met with various government officials at the invitation of the government of Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: All right. Tell me, Mr. O'Donnell, do you know Mr. Milovan Bjelica, the person Mr. Milovan Bjelica?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not believe that I've ever met that person.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Would you be so kind as to read the last paragraph of this letter, signed by Mr. Milovan Bjelica. The ERN number is 02162023. Just a couple of words. The second page that you just have in front of you.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, the paragraph reads: "The Main Board as well as any other SDS body never considered or instructed the organisation and activation of Serb people in BiH at its sessions. We were informed that such instructions were given by a certain number of retired officers of the former Yugoslav People's Army."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. So it is possible, Mr. O'Donnell, that for example, a number of military intelligence officers could be the author of this document in question, Variant A and B.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I'm going to again object to this. Mr. O'Donnell has read out the paragraph that's in the record. This is clearly the assertion by the person -- the author who signed this letter. Again, to ask Mr. O'Donnell whether this is possible or not is again not within his knowledge to say. He's already given his evidence about his corroboration of Variant A and Variant B, and he's now asking him to comment on the opinion of a SDS person he's never met.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Given the fact of the -- I mean, the professional background of Mr. O'Donnell and his experience, maybe we he can give us from this angle his opinion. I mean, without any final conclusions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: In that case, are you asking for his opinion not on the basis of the statement in this particular document?

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Yes, in general. In general, given a fact that he's very familiar and experienced in the last five years of the events in Bosnia. So maybe he can give the -- his professional opinion.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Is it possible, simply? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say it is not possible.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Mr. O'Donnell, it should be my last question. I would like to pose a question about the alleged document of Variant A and B with number 100 that you are speaking about. This is the document P3 ID. Would you be so kind to find this document in your binder, English version, of course, which is certificate translation?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have that document in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you be so kind, Mr. O'Donnell, to read the heading, actually, the title on the right upper side of this document -- left, sorry. My mistake. Left side of this document.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: On the top left-hand side of the document is written "Serbian Democratic Party of Bosnia and Herzegovina Main Board."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I assume that the author of this alleged document is the SDS of B and H Main Board. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It appears to be.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Now, Mr. O'Donnell, would you be so kind to take a short look on the last page of this document. Be so kind to read to the Chamber and to us what is the title of the -- on the -- in the middle of this page on the right -- left-hand side, please.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: At the bottom of the typing on the right-hand side is "SDS Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And we could agree that in this particular moment we are speaking about two different institutions, yes or no, Mr. O'Donnell?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot comment on that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you. That was the end of my cross-examination. Thank you for your attentions, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Any other counsel wishing to cross-examine? No? Re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. Re-examined by Ms. Reidy:

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, I am going to start my re-examination in the order of Defence counsel who cross-examined you, so my first questions will relate to the questions posed by Ms. Baen on behalf of Milan Simic. Ms. Baen inquired of you during her cross whether or not in the documents you had reviewed in your investigation, documents from Bosnia-Herzegovina usually have a stamp or a seal or a signature, and asked you whether that proposition was correct and you said, "Yes, that is correct." Can I ask you, whilst you agree that official documents usually have a stamp or a seal, in your knowledge, from examination of documents, is it the case that they always have a signature or a seal?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. That is not the case. I am aware of other documents from the Main Board issued in Bosnia, which do not have a signature or seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you -- is it possible to tell the Chamber any examples of these documents, the title of any of these documents?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: One of the documents was the instructions for voting. One of the documents --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, with all due respect, we have to object to this. We have never been presented this document which is the voting whatever document. We got two binders of the documents, which my colleagues were presenting us in -- during this hearing about the A and B document. We were never given the document which my learned colleague is now referring to to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy, which documents are these?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, with all due respect, that's not, in this particular case, my responsibility. We produced to the Defence all the documents which we intended to use. Ms. Baen in cross opened the whole subject of whether or not documents usually came with a stamp or seal. I am now asking Mr. O'Donnell of his knowledge of other documents. That document if -- I don't know whether Mr. O'Donnell has it in front of him or whether he just has a note to himself of the title, if it's available, it can be available for inspection by the Defence. It's only in my intention to be used in re-examination. It's completely appropriate that when a subject is opened by cross, that I'm entitled to re-examine on that, particularly where the evidence on the record is misleading to the full information available to the witness for consideration by the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: If I may shortly reply, Your Honours, actually, the same question was posed by Ms. Reidy just now: Does the witness say that all documents have -- which he knows are stamped and signed? He said no. Why go any further? That is the same global question that my colleague has asked the witness. If we go into a specific document, then these documents should have been -- we should have been provided with the document. Otherwise, how can we really go -- and this is a never-ending story. There might be 1.000 or 5.000 documents like that, or we can then bring some documents which are with a stamp and a signature. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy. I think you can't introduce any other documents. You can deal with the question generally.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay, Your Honour. I'm not seeking to introduce the document. I said -- because I didn't lead evidence on it, my understanding of the Rules was that it's not a document that necessarily had to be disclosed beforehand.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: But anyhow, Mr. O'Donnell, just to confirm, you do know of other documents which purport to come from the Main Board and do not bear a signature or a seal?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Is that, do you know of one document or would you say there are more than one document to your knowledge which is in the possession of the OTP?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am aware of several documents, numerous documents in the possession of the OTP which purport to come from the Main Board but which do not have a signature or seal.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. The next point I'd like to address you on is, again questions that Ms. Baen asked you with relation to whether or not portions of the Variant A/Variant B document were read out into the record, and I think so it's clear for the record, you referred to the fact that a member of the SDS Crisis Staff, Mr. Miskovic, I believe President Miskovic, read out the instructions and referred to the document. That was a document from the Prijedor municipality dated the 27th of September -- 27th of December, was it not?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, Ms. Baen then later, when apparently talking about transcripts, suggested she was referring to -- within P46 ID, to the transcript of the speech given by Mr. Karadzic which is not the document from Prijedor. So if I could just clarify it on the record, could I ask to you look at the transcript of the speech from Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have that in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: For the record that is P46 ID/11. And since there was a document Ms. Baen said she was referring to, could I ask you again to point to the reference that Mr. Karadzic makes to the Variant A/Variant B document?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Your Honours, there are several references to the contents of the document. Firstly on page 00969865, on the fifth line down, the second part of the sentence is, "We set up secret governments," which is contained in point 4 of the Variant B version of the Variant A/B document. Secondly municipal boards, which is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, if I correctly remember, yesterday it was exactly read into the transcript the whole contents referring to A and B document from this -- Mr. Karadzic's speech. I don't see the point that we are putting it again on the record. The same, completely the same thing.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, that's fine. I don't necessarily need it read into the record, but if you look back at the transcript there is a significant confusion in the examination by Ms. Baen because while she asks about one document and we discuss document 5, she then says, "Oh, no. The document I was referring to was the transcripts," without then permitting the witness to discuss the transcripts. And when we go back to look at the record and make our submissions on the admissibility, I think it must be clear that, if she was talking about the transcripts that she purported to be, that then the witness get the chance to clarify the reference in that document to the Variant A/Variant B. That wasn't done in cross. And I would like to now put on the record in re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: I think the counsel's objection is that you're merely repeating because you're asking this witness, "Could I ask you again to point out." I mean, he has already read it. So what is your question if you have a further question, please, but that --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, then I won't ask you, as my learned friend and Your Honour Judge Singh pointed out, we do have on the record these particular words, but while I think Ms. Baen had said the whole document was not read out into the record, is it your impression, from having examined these documents, that portions and references to the two, the instructions and the organisation of the Serbian people, were included in the transcript of Mr. Karadzic's speech?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, I have to object again because it calls for actual speculation again. I mean Ms. Reidy was really making this objection just five minutes ago, the same thing, impression. And document speaks for itself. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: What are you objecting to? You're saying she is asking the witness to --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm saying that this question calls for speculation because the document says for him -- for itself, because Ms. Reidy was asking for the impression of the witness, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Okay. Yes. Perhaps you can rephrase your question, Ms. Reidy. I can see the point you're trying to make but do rephrase it.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, I think you've testified that you rely on this document for corroboration as to the reliability of the Variant A/Variant B document. Could you please make it clear to the Chamber and the Bench why you so rely on the document?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Firstly, because it specifically refers to Variant A and Variant B and in total, there are five points which tie this transcript in with the Variant A and Variant B document. And I am able to point those out, should you wish.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I think you've pointed it out before. Can I ask you to -- Mr. Karadzic at the time, do you know what position he held?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Mr. Karadzic was president of the SDS in Bosnia and chairman of the Main Board of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So when Ms. Baen asked you whether any of the documents referred to provide the Chamber with any guidance as to authorship or ownership of this document, do you -- does this document give you any assistance on Ms. Baen's question?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: This calls for speculation again, Your Honour. I object to this line of questioning. It is really -- it is really focussing and -- I mean, I don't know really how to call this. This is really outrageous.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy. And I thought that the previous answer after rephrasing your question was sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'll move on then to the chain of custody documents which were given to the Defence this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated] -- ask any possible question on the -- on this point, the possible context would be to ask the witness to look at that paragraph which he read into the script, A and B variant, and ask him for his comment in respect of the question which Mr. Pantelic asked in D24/2 ID, the last page. That is the reply by the head of the SDS main office, Milovan Bjelica. "The Main Board as well as any other SDS body never considered or instructed the organisation and activation of Serb people in BiH at its sessions. We were informed that such instructions were given by a certain number of retired officers of the former Yugoslav People's Army."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. I think that is very helpful to the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: Do you understand me?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I do understand your question. Would it be helpful to clear up this matter by posing that sort of question now or to deal with it in the context of addressing Mr. Pantelic's cross, because that's where it arose, as you're suggesting?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SINGH
utterances.text: I'll leave it to you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay. I will then -- I will address it then in the context of Mr. Pantelic's -- my re-examination of Mr. Pantelic's cross-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, can I ask you just to have in front of you the four statements relating to chain of custody of a number of documents, including the Variant A/Variant B number 100. And they are D27/2 through to D30/2.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have those documents in front of me.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I'll go in chronological order that Ms. Baen went through them in, and I'll ask you about -- I think it's actually D -- D29/2. Have you got D29/2?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I believe Ms. Baen asked you whether or not there was any reference in this to the seizure of the document, and you said that there wasn't. However, can I ask you to turn to the third page of that statement with the ERN number 00570538. Do you have that? And can I ask you the visible script of the bottom of that page, is that the document P3 ID which we were discussing?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I ask you just to go back to page 2. And there -- the penultimate -- or the final paragraph before the redactions which starts with "I received the following documentation." Could I ask you just to read that into the record. And perhaps you could leave out the name which I omitted to redact on the statement.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The paragraph is as follows: "I received the following original documents from" - and then there is a name - "the custodian for documents held by the AID in November 1997 after being notified of the expected visit of investigator Bernard O'Donnell from the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Ms. Reidy, you also didn't redact the witness's signature on page 7.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you. Your Honour, I -- thank you very much. I know I didn't redact the witness's signature, because the name of this particular witness -- the person given this statement was actually on the record from yesterday. So although originally I thought it wasn't necessary, the other name, however, is -- was redacted from one of the Blank page inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. other statements. But thank you for pointing that out to me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Okay. I got confused there, in the sense that the name was redacted on the first page, so ...

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Absolutely, Your Honour. The redaction was somewhat inconsistent.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE WILLIAMS
utterances.text: Thanks.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, can I now ask you to turn to page 4 of that same document and look at 00570539. And the first paragraph under the redacted portion of the statement, could you please read that out to the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The paragraph is as follows: "At all times the documents listed above have remained under the custody and control of the AID Sarajevo. I retained those documents in my secure possession until handing them to Mr. Bernard O'Donnell at the offices of the AID Sarajevo."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I think I could speed up the proceedings by saying, is it -- is it the case that the next paragraph says that on Friday the 21st of November, the author of the statement met with yourself, produced a number of original documents, including 2(E), which is PID 3, and gave you custody of those -- of those documents?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: That, I think, covers the chain of custody with respect to the last person at AID handing them to you. And Ms. Baen went to some pains yesterday saying that she wanted to know everything about chain of custody. Again Ms. Baen asked you -- I'll take you now to document P28/2.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I ask you to turn to page 2 of that document. The ERN number is 00562505. And could I ask you to read out the paragraph just above the redacted portion.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: "In November 1997, I gave custody of the following original documents to Sejad Alimanovic after receiving an order for their handover from the Chief of Staff of the sector."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you read the next sentence, as well.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Sorry. I was just waiting for the --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Sorry.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The documents were until that time in my custody. I gave custody of the documents to Mr. Alimanovic for the purpose of providing them to the International Criminal Tribunal for the former Yugoslavia."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Could I ask you to turn to page 3 of that document and again ask you whether the visible text is a reference to PID 3.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And again, page 4. I know this is a bit time consuming, but could I ask you to read out the paragraph immediately after the redacted text.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At all times during my employment with the service for state security and the AID, the documents listed above have remained under the custody and control of those organisations. All documents held by the AID are kept in secure storage. Access to the documents is strictly controlled, and no alterations to the original documents is permitted."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. If I could go back in time again, and I'd ask you to look at D27/2 ID -- or not ID, sorry. D27/2.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I have that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. On page 3 of that is the reference at 2(E), a reference to P3 ID.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. On page 3 of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I ask you to turn to page 5 of the document. And to read out the final paragraph of -- on that page.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I can positively state that at all times whilst involved with the listing of documents, the custody of those documents was preserved by the service and access to the documents strictly controlled. I can also state that the AID has maintained a system for safeguarding the possession of documents held."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, you said that all three statements we have just gone through, you have read in full recently, and although Ms. Baen asked you whether or not those three involve particulars as to the exact seizure, you said no. Do they in fact contain a lot of information about the chain of custody of those documents, the conditions in which those documents were kept while they were under custody, and evidence as to possibility of interference with those documents following the seizure?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I now turn to the final document, which I believe is D30/2, and it was the one which does make a reference to the circumstances in which the document was seized?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Can I ask you to turn to page 6 of that statement? And can I ask you to again, I'm sorry, read on to the record that paragraph which is visible on the -- below the redacted text?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: "I can positively state that at all times whilst I held the position of Deputy Chief of Staff, State Security Sarajevo, a system was in place to ensure that all documents were maintained in secure custody of the service. I can also state that since that time, the AID has maintained a system for safeguarding the possession of documents held. I can therefore state that at all times the documents listed above have remained under the custody and control of state security and the AID Sarajevo."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And could I just -- rather than, as I said, based on the fact that you have read all these statements, and rather than waste time itemising the reference in every single one, could you tell us whether you have information, having read these statements, as to some of the conditions under which documents were then held in the -- by the AID from the time of seizure in 1992 through to the handing over of that document to you in November, 1997?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Could I ask you if you could briefly just indicate what those -- the information that document contains that would go to showing chain of -- conditions of chain of custody which was at issue -- raised as an issue in cross?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The documents from the time of coming into the possession of state security and later the AID, were kept secure by that service. Documents were kept in secure storage. Access to the documents was strictly limited. And custody over the documents was maintained throughout the entire period. The first -- sorry, the last statement, D30-2, although not being able to state the person's name who was responsible for seizing the document, he was able to state positively that it was seized by someone under his command, and he was familiar with that document coming into the service.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Objection. The document speaks for itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, the document does speak for itself but the whole issue of chain of custody and every detail relating to it and all those issues were not -- were put into question by the Defence, and now we are simply asking Mr. O'Donnell to comment on those aspects of security, of access, of those things which he can comment on, having reread the statements he took from the AID staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Document 32 is in evidence, we have three professional Judges here who can read and decide, make their own opinion as to what the statement means. This gentleman here just gave opinion testimony on what a statement is already in evidence means. That's a comment on the evidence which is what the Judges' function is, is to make their own decision, determination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: He's not making any conclusions at all. Ms. Reidy, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, if you'd -- you have provided some information that's contained. If there were further details on what steps were taken to secure the chain of custody that you -- or information that you would like to put on the record, can I ask to you finish the evidence you were giving?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The document was signed over to me on the 21st of November. There was an official receipt prepared. That receipt was placed in the envelope which was still in the envelope yesterday when I unsealed the document for the Court. The document was transferred by myself from Sarajevo to The Hague and lodged into evidence by myself, where it has remained since that time.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I think I've finished dealing with the question of the chain of custody documents and the evidence they provide as to security of the document. Again, although this was a course of questioning that eventually Ms. Baen desisted from, I would like to ask you one question on re-examination as to a number of handwritten annotations on various copies of the Variant A/Variant B in our possession, which Ms. Baen asked you to direct your attention to. Having given -- having been asked about handwritten annotations, can I ask you whether or not there were any of those handwritten annotations which, in your examination, provide again information that could be considered to be taken into account as to the reliability of the document?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Of the copies that we have in the OTP, and that have been mentioned, 47, 55 --

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I really don't want to keep objecting because I know, as I said, I want to finish this, but it calls for a legal conclusion. The purpose of this hearing is for the Judges to decide the reliability of the document, and it invades the province of the Trial Chamber when the witness is giving that opinion testimony.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honours, Ms. Baen wanted the witness to comment and draw the Chamber's attention to certain handwritten annotations until she desisted from that line of questioning. I think in redirect, as it's opened, I'm allowed to direct the witness to one of those handwritten annotations, in terms of reliability, which is -- Ms. Baen's argument was that this is somehow unreliable. On re-examination, I simply want to again draw attention to one of them with respect to the reliability of the document, and I think that should be a permissible question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The objection is overruled, Ms. Baen. Ms. Reidy, you can go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, to speed this up, could I ask you to turn to what I hope is number 6 of P45 ID?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have that document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Does the Chamber have in front of them P45 ID? If I'm dealing with the right bundle, that should be a document with the ERN number in the corner on the page SA 032072. I hope that's the same document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, is that the --

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Could I ask you to turn to the final page of that document, which is SA 032082?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Does that page contain some form of handwritten annotation?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: To the best of your knowledge, is that handwritten annotation in existence on any of the other copies, 47, 55, 93, 96, 100, 101/3 or 104?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. I would ask -- attached to that page, I believe, is the translation of those annotation notes?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And have you made any investigation into what those handwritten notes may be?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The handwritten notes at the first part appears to be a subdistribution of copy 93, 93A, 93B, 93C and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Could I ask, out of your examination of 47, 55, 93, 96, 100, 101/3, and 104, do many of the different versions have unique handwritten annotations on them?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, they do. Your Honours, all of those copies, apart from one photocopy of 93, have handwritten notations.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. And the handwritten notations on each of those are distinct? They're different? They're not the same annotations on 47 as on 101/3, for example?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. The notations on 47 are different from all of the others; the notations on 55 are different from all the others; 93 are different from all the others; 96 are different from the others; and 104 is different from all others.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, Judge Singh did pose a question at the end of yesterday's hearing which he asked the witness to address. It just strikes me with this last question that -- I don't know whether this is an appropriate time for the witness to -- to answer it. I could repose the question of Mr. -- of Your Honour Judge Singh and have that answered.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Specifically, with relation to copy 100 ID -- P3 ID, you were asked yesterday to compare the copies that bear the number "100" in the corner with the original which you had kept sealed in the envelope. And Mr. -- Your Honour Judge Singh asked you to provide your impression for what it was worth as to whether or not those were reproductions in photocopy form or other form of the document in the sealed envelope. And I was wondering if having examined the document and handwritten annotations on it you could answer Your Honour's inquiry.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Certainly. Your Honour, I compared the document which was in the sealed envelope opened yesterday with other copies that we have of that document numbered 100. The copies that I compared with it were the ones starting firstly with 00184274; and secondly, 00270657; and thirdly, SA 006218. Each of those three appeared to be photocopies of the first document.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I've finished my cross on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I have to objected to this, because as far as I know, our witness is not an expert witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: -- who can say or claim that these are the exact photocopies. So I object to this, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm repeating Your Honour Judge Singh's questions, and Your Honour Judge Singh did specifically say "for what it's worth." And again, I said to the witness "for what it's worth." We appreciate that the opinion is offered not as an expert witness but as someone who has studied the documents simply in response to a request from the Bench.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: As long as there is an instruction that goes along with his answer in the record that he's not an expert and this is a layperson's opinion, then that's fine; otherwise, we object and ask a motion to strike that answer until he is shown the proper predicate for giving an expert opinion on that. And this is really, really important. And if we're going to go into that, we need to open this back up and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no. Ms. Baen, the point was made by your colleague, and it's taken. We don't need to repeat that.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Well, it's just real important, Your Honour, that the record speaks, because if these men are convicted, and this document comes into evidence and is used against them -- this is a huge issue, Your Honour, and we're just doing our jobs protecting the record.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, I didn't say that. The point was taken by your colleague when he made the objection.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: But we need a ruling on the objection in order to prepare it for appeal.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: If I say the point is taken, that means the objection is sustained.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Reidy.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I -- may I just seek the consequences of the -- the objection being sustained means that it is inappropriate for the witness to respond to the question posed yesterday. Is that it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. What he says is -- what the Defence are saying, this witness is not an expert.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Absolutely. But --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: And you did say that the question was -- Judge Singh did say for whatever it's worth. Let's end there. All right?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: All right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Please proceed with other questions.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: All right. And I think the record reflects the nature of the answer. I am now finished with cross-examination conducted by Ms. Baen, and I'd now just like to ask a few question relating to the cross conducted by Mr. Pantelic on behalf of Blagoje Simic. And my redirect will focus exclusively on the document which he was anxious to have in B/C/S, that is, D23/1. And I say -- I myself, and I think for the Bench, will be using the English version of that document. I will start with the point raised by Your Honour Judge Singh.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: You were asked by Mr. Pantelic to comment on the final paragraph of that letter which says: "We were informed that such instructions were given by a certain number of retired officers of the former Yugoslav People's Army." Can I ask whether possession in your information -- information in your possession or information about which you've testified here -- let me -- I apologise. I'd just like to rephrase the question. When Mr. Pantelic asked you the question, he also then -- he asked you to comment on whether or not it was possible that military intelligence officers had constructed, I think, the document. And you had said it's not possible. And I'd like you to, please, explain why you say you don't think it's possible. And if there's any information that you have which would contradict the fact that it's not from the SDS but from a certain number of retired officers from the former Yugoslav People's Army.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: The question that I was asked, as I recall, was whether it was possible that the document -- the instructions --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm so sorry, Your Honour, but this goes for the -- "and you had said you don't think it's possible." It's again calling for a conclusion by this witness. I'm sorry, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I believe --

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Yes. This is the interpretation of the document which was disclosed to us by the OTP. We offered -- my colleague Pantelic offered the document to the evidence. I don't really -- you know, with all due respect, I really see no point that we go again into interpreting the document by the witness who wasn't writing this document. So if we want to have somebody to interpret that document, why don't we bring the person who wrote the document so that he can tell us what did he mean with this sentence. That is my objection. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Let me ask Ms. Reidy, what is the point of your question?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Well, the point is twofold, Your Honour. One, it was Mr. Pantelic who asked about the possibility of the document having been - I believe the word was "drafted" - by military intelligence officers. That was objected to as speculation. It was -- the objection was overruled. The question was put to the witness, and the witness said, "It is not possible." I'm only seeking in redirect to know the basis of the answer, as Mr. Pantelic did not pursue it. That would be the firstfold. The secondfold would be to try to place in the appropriate context the evidence which the witness has already testified as to Mr. Karadzic's words and the statement here, which is on the record, as I believe that Judge Singh was suggesting might be an appropriate way for me to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: If I may, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Pantelic.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Very briefly. If we are going step by step with the standards possible or not possible, what is -- if not possible, I mean, we are going in the really hypothetical area. That's --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No, no, no, no. Mr. Pantelic, I think Ms. Reidy has explained the point of her question, and I'll allow her to proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, just let me go back. You answered to Mr. Pantelic that it was not -- that in your opinion, it was not possible. And all I want to know is the basis for your answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: And Your Honours, sorry. I withdraw this question, so I don't see any basis for redirect. It wasn't my question. I said I withdraw my question. So it's -- it's in the record.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honours. I don't know if you could -- if you're interested in scrolling back, but it's page 54 of today's evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps you can --

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: And it is line -- it goes on -- the line is page 4, Mr. Pantelic's question. There's a lot of preceding stuff. It says -- okay. "In general, given the fact that he's very familiar, experienced in the last five years of the events in Bosnia, so maybe he can give the -- his professional opinion. Is it possible, simply? Yes or no?"

utterances.speaker: MR. O'DONNELL
utterances.text: "I would say it is not possible."

utterances.speaker: MR. PANTELIC
utterances.text: "Thank you. Now, Mr. O'Donnell, it should be my last question." The question is not withdrawn. It's clearly on the record. And I should be allowed to re-examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. It is another question that was withdrawn, not this particular one.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, if you could now answer -- give reason for the basis to that answer that's been re-read on the transcript.

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd say that it is not possible that the document be -- was drafted by a number of retired officers of the former Yugoslav People's Army, because the document is referred to in other documents which have been located right across Bosnia, in a spread across Bosnia. Another copy of the document has been found by the International Stabilisation Force. Some of the documents which refer to it we got from the Bosnian Serbs - we obtained them officially - some through the execution of search warrants that were conducted by the Office of the Prosecutor, another from the Autonomous Region of Krajina, officially, to members of the Office of the Prosecutor, and others during missions that I was involved in to the Republika Srpska government in Pale. The other factor is that although it is stated in that document that the Main Board was not involved - I'll read it: "The Main Board, as well as any other SDS body, never considered or instructed the organisation and activity of Serb people at its sessions" - Mr. Karadzic himself makes clear reference to the Variant A and Variant B at the time that he was president of the SDS. At the time that these instructions came out, as I understand it, he was chairman of the Main Board, who purportedly issued the instructions.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I was hoping that he would not testify to this, trying to interpret a document because now I have to make a request. And I know it was not the fault of any of these prosecutors because I like and trust every one of them -- it was no fault of their own that we just got this document today that we are talking about. But first of all, under rules of reciprocal discovery, those of us with reciprocal discovery should have received these documents. Also under rules --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Which documents?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: The document which says -- the letter that says from the SDS, D23/1, that calls into question the authenticity of any Variant A/B document. This is going to violate Rule 67, mandatory disclosures, Rule 68, reciprocal disclosures, and arguably this is exculpatory information since the number one document the OTP is trying to use against our clients, this Variant A/B document, has been called -- the authenticity the has been called into question through correspondence with the OTP. Therefore -- I want to be reasonable. We didn't object to this witness testifying even though he wasn't on their witness list. We didn't object to going forward based on these four statements that were given to us yesterday in the middle of the hearing that was about these statements. All we are going to have to ask for now is the opportunity to get this witness who prepared this letter from the SDS, who says the SDS didn't write these -- didn't author these A/B documents, we have to get him here to complete all the information with respect to these documents before the Trial Chamber can make a determination on admissibility. And -- because the alleged author, as Judge Singh pointed out yesterday, it says "SDS" at the top, the document purports to say that the SDS, they were the people who authored this document. Now we get a document today from the OTP that says, from the SDS, "We never did this. Some retired personnel from the JNA did it." That's pretty important for us to know for purposes of this hearing. That's the whole question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Baen, you finished your submission?

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: On the request to have the witnesses and the violations under the rules, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: All right. Ms. Reidy, can you continue?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, I don't want to address this now. May we have an opportunity to respond to any request by Ms. Baen in writing, in terms of our submissions on the whole -- on this issue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: No. I think you can respond orally.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Right now? Would you like me to do that now or would you like me to finish the re-examination?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You finish the re-examination first.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, again this document which the Defence asked to be put into evidence and which has been entered into evidence on the request of the Defence, could I ask you to turn to the first page of it? This is document 23/1, and it bears the ERN number in the corner 02162022, it is the first page of the controversial paragraph we just discussed. Could I ask you to read out the second -- the second, third and fourth sentences of that first paragraph?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: "SDS archives do not contain documents you asked for because they remained in the SDS main office in Djuro Djakovic Street in Sarajevo. Minutes of meetings of the SDS Main Board and the executive board dated from 12 July, 1990, through April, 1992, were stored in the above-mentioned premises. We think that all documents are with the BiH Federation Ministry of Interior because they were the first to enter the SDS premises when the staff had to leave the office and the town of Sarajevo."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that information consistent with the information you have as to the seizure of document PI -- P -- ID -- P3 ID?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: And can I ask you, then, to turn to the second paragraph of that same page, and the penultimate or the second-last sentence of that, which starts with, "As far as we know"?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: "As far as we know, access to this documentation was provided by Ms. Rajka Stanisic, then the employee of the national -- sorry, of the Republika Srpska National Assembly."

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this reflect your evidence of the mission that you have testified to undertaking to Pale and having spoken with Mrs. Stanisic as to her cooperation with you on talking about documents and giving the -- well, you and your colleagues on the mission access?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it does, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Thank you very much. That's the final question on --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Mr. Zecevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honours, if I correctly remembered, the witness testified to the fact that Ms. Rajka Stanisic gave him the minutes of the 50th session of Republika Srpska -- of the Assembly of Republika Srpska, and he never ever stated that he received any copy of any document, whether 100, 055, 47, or whichever of the copies that they have in his possession on the -- concerning the document P3 ID. He never testified that he received that document from Ms. Rajka Stanisic. And now it appears from the transcript that he actually received these documents from Ms. Rajka Stanisic. So whether my learned colleague can clarify that or whether the witness was not telling us the truth yesterday when he was stating -- when he was giving his testimony in the -- in direct, thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Would the Chamber be -- would it be assisted if I --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you respond?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: -- finished my question or explored that?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Can you respond?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: I can respond, yes. The question was not meant, nor was that sentence, referring to a copy of Variant A/Variant B. It was access to documentation. The witness here testified that he had gone to Pale on mission, that there had been cooperation from the Republika Srpska authorities, and he himself had spoken with Rajka Stanisic. Mr. Pantelic specifically asked him about whether or not he had gone to Pale, whether or not he had met with Rajka Stanisic, et cetera, and I'm simply asking him whether or not this letter goes to corroborating his letter that they were shown cooperation with access to documentation in general while they were in Pale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Then you may rephrase your question.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: Mr. O'Donnell, could I ask to you clarify the cooperation which you've testified to -- well, the cooperation coming from Mrs. Stanisic and other RS officials with relation to access to documentation, does that refer to documents such as the transcripts of the assembly documentation or does it refer to copies of Variant A/Variant B?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: It refers to the transcript of the 50th assembly session of the Republika Srpska along with a large quantity of other documentation.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: So just so it's clear, you did -- did you at that -- during that mission, in, I believe it was 1998, were you presented with a copy of Variant A/Variant B by Mrs. Stanisic?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we were not.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: But you were given access to other documentation, including the transcripts of the 50th assembly?

utterances.speaker: BERNARD O'DONNELL [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is correct. We obtained copies of that documentation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: You are through?

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Sorry, Your Honour, yes. That's the end of the re-examination.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, because I was thinking about these documents, P46 and P45, yes, because I thought that they should be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Given the fact that the Defence exhibits are in evidence, we would seek to have P45 and P46 now entered into evidence after they've been discussed on the record, and they be fully admitted into evidence, subject, if the Bench wishes, to P46, 7 and 8 remaining with the ID status until the final translation comes through, because they were the two documents out of the 11 subdocuments which only had draft translations.

utterances.speaker: MS. BAEN
utterances.text: I think I speak on behalf of all the Defence counsel when we say we object to the admission of these documents for this reason: It was settled on several occasions last fall that the one document that we were having the admissibility and the authentication hearing on was PID 3. They have tried to focus on the history, the chain of custody, for whatever it's worth, of PID 3. On all these other documents in these collections, they have not even attempted to prove up chain of custody. We have not cross-examined on it because the agreement from day one was that we were focusing on the one document that was obtained in the SDS headquarters supposedly in Sarajevo in 1992. That has been so crystal clear from the very beginning, we vehemently object to any of these documents just being put into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: The objection is overruled. The Trial Chamber has decided that these two, P46, excluding the P3 ID, will be admitted into evidence, and P45 as well, and also the document that was used for cross-examination by the Defence, that is D31/2, the English as well as the Serbo-Croat, D31/2 ter, because the Trial Chamber believes it has probative value. We will adjourn until tomorrow at 1415. MR. DI FAZIO: If Your Honours please, may I just raise one very brief issue? I think this pretty well completes the evidence relating to the introduction of this particular document, the contentious document, I'll say. Do you want to have submissions from us on its final admissibility? And if so, may I propose that we do that on Thursday, and as my colleague states, possibly in writing as well?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes, there is a motion by the Defence to call a witness, as they put it on record, so the Trial Chamber has to decide that first before we can decide on whether or not you can make oral submissions, but definitely whatever continuation material we have on this issue will have to be after the witness tomorrow. MR. DI FAZIO: But one way or the other, you want to hear submissions on this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. We will have submissions, of course, orally.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry just on that, you did indicate earlier I would be able to respond to the oral motion raised -- respond orally to the motion raised by Ms. Baen, and I would just like to know what would be the most appropriate time to do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: After the witness tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: After the witness tomorrow. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. The Trial Chamber is very concerned about the request on this witness.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: So we can deliberate on this matter further after the witness tomorrow is completed.

utterances.speaker: MS. REIDY
utterances.text: Very clear. Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, completely different matter. My client is not feeling well and he would like to waive his presence for tomorrow. I have to inform the Trial Chamber that I have done everything that was up to me concerning the videolink, but as I understood, it is not as yet clear whether this videolink or the communication between me and my client will be via the laptop, which was suggested by the Registry, or the mobile phone and the phone over here, which was suggested by you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Firstly, it will be by mobile phone to yourself from your client until the laptop connections are completed.

utterances.speaker: MR. ZECEVIC
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you, Your Honours. In any case, my client is waiving his right of presence for tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: For tomorrow, all right, thank you. So we will continue our proceedings tomorrow at 1415 hours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Yes. I was just reminded that Mr. O'Donnell is through. You are free to leave.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
utterances.text: Because the cross-examination and the re-examination has been completed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MUMBA
